message.content:
For a reflection through a plane with unit normal vector \(\mathbf n\), the reflection matrix is  
\[
R=I-2\mathbf n\mathbf n^T.
\]
Thus \(I-R\) is proportional to \(\mathbf v\mathbf v^T\), where \(\mathbf v\) is any normal vector to the plane.

Compute:
\[
I-R=
\begin{pmatrix}
\frac{4}{15} & -\frac{2}{15} & -\frac{2}{3}\\
-\frac{2}{15} & \frac{1}{15} & \frac{1}{3}\\
-\frac{2}{3} & \frac{1}{3} & \frac{5}{3}
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
Multiply by \(15\):
\[
15(I-R)=
\begin{pmatrix}
4 & -2 & -10\\
-2 & 1 & 5\\
-10 & 5 & 25
\end{pmatrix}
=
\begin{pmatrix}
2\\
-1\\
-5
\end{pmatrix}
\begin{pmatrix}
2 & -1 & -5
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
So a normal vector is
\[
\begin{pmatrix}
2\\
-1\\
-5
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
This has first coordinate positive and gcd \(=1\).

The answer is \(\begin{pmatrix}2\\-1\\-5\end{pmatrix}\).
